testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You are braking on dry pavement at 55 mph. How much distance does brake lag add to your total stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your total stopping distance.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with a dual brake system, what should you do?

options.text: Let the vehicle warm up before driving to make sure fuel reaches the engine.
Wait until the air compressor builds at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems before driving.
Start driving right after the vehicle starts.
Pump the pedal about 20 times to build pressure, then start driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the air compressor builds at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air system, wait for the air compressor to build at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: What do ABS brakes do?

options.text: Help prevent your wheels from locking up.
Stop your vehicle from speeding up on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help prevent your wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) prevent your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on a slippery surface.

questions.question: During a static leakage test, what is the maximum safe air leakage rate for a double combination vehicle?
questions.explanation: For a double combination vehicle with air brakes, the leakage rate should not exceed 3 psi in one minute. If air leaks faster than this, the vehicle needs repairs and should not be driven.

questions.question: What is a wig wag?

options.text: A low air pressure warning device
A tube that carries air to the brakes
A type of air brake system

questions.correctAnswerText: A low air pressure warning device
questions.explanation: A wig wag is a low air pressure warning device. It drops a mechanical arm into your view if tank pressure drops between 55 and 75 psi. All air brake vehicles must have a low pressure warning device.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have anti-lock brakes. Other air brake vehicles built on or after March 1, 1998 must also have them.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: What type of force must emergency brakes use?
questions.explanation: Emergency brakes in an air brake system must use mechanical force. Air pressure can leak away over time, so mechanical force is needed to hold the brakes on.

questions.question: When going down a steep hill, what should you do?

options.text: Put the vehicle in a low gear and use engine braking
Downshift often instead of using the brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the vehicle in a low gear and use engine braking
questions.explanation: On long or steep hills, mainly use engine braking to control your speed. Use your brakes only to help slow you down.

questions.question: How do you use the stab braking method in an emergency?

options.text: Apply the brakes fully until the wheels lock, release until the wheels roll, then repeat
Apply the brakes halfway while keeping the wheels rolling
Fully apply the brakes, lock the wheels, and hold the pedal until the vehicle stops

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes fully until the wheels lock, release until the wheels roll, then repeat
questions.explanation: The stab braking method involves fully applying the brakes until they lock. Then release the brakes until the wheels start rolling again. Repeat this process until the vehicle stops.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, what can a separate air tank be used for?

options.text: Make the air brakes work more effectively.
Charge the brakes on the rear trailer.

questions.explanation: In vehicles with dual parking control valves, a separate air tank can temporarily release the spring brakes if they activate due to low air pressure. Pushing the correct control will release the spring brakes for a short time. This lets the driver move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: What happens if brake pads rub against brake drums and create too much heat?

options.text: The brakes will become extra sensitive.
The air compressor will turn on to cool the brakes.

questions.explanation: Brakes get hot when used. If they get too hot from overuse, they expand and change chemically. This makes them less effective and can cause them to stop working completely. This is called "brake fade."

questions.question: The ____ are turned on by an electric switch that the brake pedal triggers.
questions.explanation: In a vehicle with air brakes, the brake lights turn on when you press the brake pedal. The air pressure moves an electric switch that turns on the brake lights.

questions.question: What type of force do emergency brakes use?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three parts: the service brake, the parking brake, and the emergency brake. Emergency and parking brakes use mechanical force.

questions.question: An air compressor governor stops pumping air when the air tanks reach what pressure level?
questions.explanation: An air compressor governor stops pumping when the air tanks reach 125 psi. This pressure level is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: What color are the ABS warning lamps?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have yellow warning lamps.

questions.question: When should service brakes be tested?
questions.explanation: Always test your service brakes before driving. Testing them before a trip helps you find any problems before you need to brake on the road.

questions.question: How do you test the low pressure warning signal?

options.text: Turn the parking brake on and off.
Press and release the brake pedal quickly.
Disconnect and reconnect all glad hands.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and release the brake pedal quickly.
questions.explanation: Your low pressure warning light must work properly. After the system fills with air, test the warning signal by pressing and releasing the brake pedal quickly. This releases air from the system. The warning signal should turn on when pressure drops to a dangerous level.

questions.question: What does a one-way check valve do?

options.text: Drain water and compressor oil from the air tanks.
Prevent air from escaping if the air compressor leaks.
Activate the emergency brakes when there is a leak.
Hold the spring brakes in place until they are used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent air from escaping if the air compressor leaks.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve must be placed between the air compressor and the first main air tank. This valve stops air from leaving the system if the air compressor develops a leak.

questions.question: In an S-cam brake, friction happens when the brake shoes and linings do what?

options.text: Press against the outside of the brake drum.
Press against the inside of the brake drum.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: Friction in a brake drum is created when brake shoes and linings press against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: A ____ lets a driver slowly apply spring brakes.
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets a driver slowly apply spring brakes. In trucks with this system, a lever on the dashboard controls the valve.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure gets too low in an air brake system?

options.text: The brakes will be very sensitive.

questions.explanation: If air pressure in an air brake system gets too low, the brakes will stop working. Pressing the brake pedal too often releases air faster than the compressor can replace it.

questions.question: Why do you need to drain air tanks regularly?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs to be replaced
Because compressed air contains some water which must be drained from the tanks
To allow for a change in air pressure
To remove bad air from the tanks

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains some water which must be drained from the tanks
questions.explanation: Compressed air in an air brake system contains water and oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up in the system. You must drain the tanks regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: When you push the brake pedal, air brakes work:

options.text: Only if it is warm outside.

questions.explanation: Air takes time to travel through the brake lines. There is a delay of at least half a second between pressing the brake pedal and the brakes starting to work.

questions.question: On a truck with air brakes, the air compressor:

options.text: Pumps air into the air storage tanks.
Moves air to the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks. The air compressor governor controls when the compressor runs.
